questions: I'm new, where do I begin?
answers.answer:
Duracash makes sure finished work gets billed with everything the customer needs, then follows the money until it's paid.
- Jobs, New job: job name, address, customer, who pays you and the contract amount. The rest can wait under More details (optional).
- Put the contract, photos and tickets on the job record (Take a photo or Add a file), or bring emails and texts in through the Inbox.
- Progress pay app: enter this draw, the total done so far or a percent, then Draft progress pay app. Duracash holds back retainage and lists the paperwork the customer needs.
- Add each missing document, then Review & send. It can go once nothing is missing.
- Record a payment when it arrives, send the waiver, ask for retainage at the end, then Finish job.
Today shows what needs you next.

questions: How do I create a job?
How do I add a new job?
Where do I enter a contract?
answers.answer: Go to Jobs and tap New job. Fill in Job name, Address, Customer, Who pays you? and Contract amount ($), then tap Save job. More details (optional) holds Contract number, Retainage % (if the contract holds money back), Phone, Who signs off on your bills, Email for pay apps and Notes (kept on the job record); all of them can wait. A customer you have saved before keeps its details; change them in Settings, Customer settings.
follow_ups: What does Who pays you? mean?
How do I bill progress on a job?

questions: How do I edit a job?
I made a typo in the job name
How do I delete a job?
Can I change the contract amount?
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Edit job, next to its name. You can change the job name, address, contract number and Retainage % (a new retainage applies from the next pay app). The contract amount can change only before the first pay app and without a schedule of values; after that, use a change order. The job code stays the same. Tap Save changes. Who signs off, the email for pay apps and the paperwork list are in Settings, Customer settings. In the Edit job form an owner also sees Delete job. It shows while the job has no payments and no pay app other than a deleted draft, so tap Delete draft first if one is open. If a pay app was sent or a payment came in, finish the job instead.

questions: What does Who pays you? mean?
What does the role field mean?
What is the role on a new job?
answers.answer: Who pays you? says what kind of customer this is. The homeowner or property owner: you bill them directly. A general contractor (you are the sub): you bill a GC. It sets the paperwork a new customer starts with: a GC usually needs a lien waiver, an insurance certificate and daily tickets with every pay app. Change it in Settings, Customer settings.

questions: Can I use this on my phone?
answers.answer: There's no app-store app. Duracash runs in your phone's browser: sign in at the same address, and add it to your home screen from the browser's menu or Share button. On a phone, Take a photo opens the camera, in the Inbox, on a job and on the paperwork page, so you can photograph tickets straight onto a job.
follow_ups: How do I import emails and texts?

questions: Can I add my office manager?
How do I invite my bookkeeper?
Can more than one person log in?
answers.answer: Yes. An owner opens Settings, Team, enters Their email, picks They join as (Member or Owner) and taps Invite. Members draft pay apps, record payments and add paperwork. Owners also send, delete drafts, finish jobs, and manage the team, the inbound addresses, reset and deleting the company. To let members send, an owner turns on Members can send pay apps, lien waivers and retainage requests in Settings, Company. Every action is in the Activity log with the person's name. If the invite can't be emailed, the owner gets a link to pass on; it works once, for 7 days.

questions: What's the difference between a pay app and an invoice?
Can I get a PDF of the pay app?
answers.answer: A pay app (pay application) is the bill for work done this period. It lists what was completed, line by line if the job has a schedule of values, adds signed change orders, and holds back retainage. Many contracts also need paperwork with it. Open any pay app and tap Open the PDF; the same PDF goes with the email when you send it. If your company bills homeowners in draws (Settings, Company, How you bill), the app says draw instead of pay app.
follow_ups: What is paperwork?
What is retainage?

questions: How do I bill progress on a job?
How do I make a progress pay app?
Bill for work done this month
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Progress pay app. Without a schedule of values, pick This draw $ (the work since the last pay app), Total done so far $ or % complete, and enter it; the line below shows what the pay app comes to. With a schedule of values, enter how much of each line is done to date. Tap Draft progress pay app. Duracash holds back retainage and lists the paperwork from the customer's settings. The job stays in progress.
follow_ups: What is paperwork?
What is a draft for their review?

questions: How do I mark a job done?
The job is finished, what now?
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Mark done (under More if you don't see it). Fill in Anything to note? (optional) and Period to, tap Confirm done, then confirm. Duracash drafts the final pay app for everything not billed yet. If a draft is already open, send it or tap Delete draft first; the message names it. A job with retainage also gets closeout paperwork for the punch list. Marked done by mistake? Undo done works until the final pay app goes out.
follow_ups: How do I get retainage released?

questions: How do I send a pay app?
What does Fix things before sending mean?
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Review & send. The pay app page shows Before you send: who it goes to, Also email (CC), the amount, the subject and what is attached; Open the PDF to check it. If your company address, phone or licence number is blank, it says so there with a Company details button; you can still send. Then tap Approve & send to. While paperwork is missing or an unsigned change order is on the pay app, the job shows Fix N things before sending (or Add N missing documents, or Get CO N signed) instead. It goes to the customer's Email for pay apps with the PDF and paperwork attached, from your company name, and replies come back to you. Only owners send, unless an owner turns on Members can send in Settings, Company. Money, Outbox shows whether it was delivered.
follow_ups: What is paperwork?
Did the customer get my pay app?

questions: What is a draft for their review?
How do I send a pencil draft?
Can the GC review before I submit?
answers.answer: A draft for their review (pencil copy) is the draft pay app sent to the customer to agree quantities and change orders before the real one, so nothing gets pushed to next month. It's optional. With a draft open, tap Send draft for their review on the job. If you don't see it, look under More. When they answer, tap Customer agreed to the draft, or Customer wants changes and note what they said.
follow_ups: How do I send a pay app?

questions: How do I delete a draft pay app?
answers.answer: Open the job, tap Delete draft (under More) and confirm; only an owner can. The draft stays in the pay app list as Cancelled, any change order on it comes off, and you can draft again from the job page. The newest pay app on an open job can be withdrawn instead, if it was sent and nothing is paid on it (delete any newer draft first): an owner taps Pull back this pay app… on the pay app page, and the customer is emailed that nothing is due on it.

questions: Why can't I draft a pay app?
answers.answer: Nothing to draft means all finished work is already on a pay app. Enter more progress with Progress pay app, or tap Mark done first. If a draft is already open, Duracash says so and names it.

questions: What is a schedule of values?
Line items on a pay app
Can I bill by quantity and unit rate?
How do I set up a schedule of values?
Bill by quantities and unit rates
Import my schedule of values from Excel
answers.answer: A schedule of values breaks the contract into lines: a quantity at a unit rate (or a lump sum), with overhead and profit on top. Before the first pay app, open the job and tap Set up schedule of values. Paste rows straight from Excel, Google Sheets, a CSV or your estimate PDF and tap Read pasted rows, or type them; then tap Save schedule. The total has to equal the contract. Each progress pay app then asks how much of each line is done to date and bills the difference line by line, like an AIA G703 continuation sheet. Signed change orders add their own lines.

questions: Why does a pay app need a packet?
answers.answer: Paperwork is everything the contract says must go with a pay app: lien waivers, delivery tickets, photos, signed change orders, schedule of values, insurance certificate. Duracash lists the items from the customer's settings (Paperwork needed with each pay app) and won't send the pay app until each one is in. See it in the Paperwork column of Money, Pay apps, or tap Open paperwork on the job.
follow_ups: How do I add missing paperwork?
How do I change what a customer needs?

questions: How do I add missing paperwork?
How do I clear a packet item?
How do I mark something present?
How do I attach a document to the packet?
What does I have this mean?
answers.answer:
On the job, tap Add N missing documents (or Fix N things before sending, or Open paperwork). For each missing item:
- Take a photo or Choose file: it goes on the job record and is attached in one step.
- Choose a record… from the job record, then Attach.
- I have this…: say where it is (optional, for example "emailed to the GC on 10/12"), then Save.
- Not needed for this customer, if they never need it.
Remove takes an item back off while the pay app is a draft. The Activity log shows how each item was handled.
follow_ups: How do I import emails and texts?

questions: How do I change what a customer needs?
How do I change what a payer requires?
Who signs off on my bills?
What is the email for pay apps?
answers.answer: Settings, Customer settings keeps each customer's rules. Open a customer to change Who signs off on your bills, Email for pay apps, Days between follow-ups, Days they usually take to pay, Paperwork needed with each pay app (separated by commas), They send pay apps back when, Also email (CC) and more, then tap Save customer. New pay apps use the paperwork list. When a customer sends a pay app back, add the reason to They send pay apps back when and tap Save customer. While something is blocking send on a job, you can also note it there under Customer sent a pay app back? Note why.

questions: How do I add a change order?
Extra work the customer asked for
answers.answer: Open the job and tap New change order (or use the form on Money, Change orders). Enter a Title and Amount ($), negative for a credit, and tap Create change order. It stays Unsigned until the customer signs: tap Request signature to email them a signing link, or Signed on paper… and Take a photo of the signed copy. Once signed it is billable on the next pay app, even after the job is done.
follow_ups: Can I bill an unsigned change order?
The customer won't sign the change order

questions: Can I bill an unsigned change order?
Put a change order on the pay app before it's signed
Can I bill a change order that isn't signed yet?
Change order not signed, can I bill it?
answers.answer: Yes. On the job's Change orders card, tap Bill now (send waits for signature) on the unsigned change order while no draft is open. Its dollars go on the next pay app, but that pay app can't be sent until the change order is signed: the job shows Get CO N signed. An unsigned change order never goes out by accident.

questions: The customer won't sign the change order
answers.answer: Tap Withdraw on the unsigned change order and confirm. If it is on an open draft, an owner deletes that draft first (Delete draft), then withdraw the change order and draft again. A withdrawn change order stays in history.

questions: How do I record a payment?
The customer paid, what do I do?
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Record a payment. Pick the Pay app, check Amount received ($) (it starts at what is owed), Date received and Check or reference no. (optional), then tap Record. Less than owed leaves the pay app Partly paid; paid in full opens the waiver step for that pay app. The amount can't be more than what is owed, and a reference can only be used once per job. Many payments at once? Read a QuickBooks export on Money, Payments.
follow_ups: What is a lien waiver?
Does it connect to QuickBooks?

questions: They only paid part of it
They paid only part of the pay app
Customer paid less than the bill
answers.answer: Record what came in with Record a payment. The pay app shows Partly paid with the rest still owed, and no waiver is due until it's paid in full. Follow up on the balance from Money, Unpaid. If the rest won't come, an owner taps Accept $X short pay…, gives the reason and confirms.

questions: Why do I need a waiver?
answers.answer: A lien waiver gives up your lien rights for money you've been paid. Conditional: it only takes effect if the payment clears. Unconditional: payment received. Some states require exact statutory forms, so use the form your state or the customer requires; Duracash doesn't write it.
follow_ups: How do I send a waiver?

questions: How do I send a waiver?
answers.answer: When a pay app is paid in full, the job shows Choose waiver and send (Today shows Waiver due). Put your signed waiver on the job record first (kind: Lien waiver), or tap Take a photo on the waiver page. Pick the type; the line under it says when it fits. Then tap Approve & send. The email attaches the newest lien waiver on the job record; with none, it tells the customer the signed waiver follows separately. One waiver per paid pay app, and only after the payment is recorded. Duracash doesn't write waiver forms; states set them.
follow_ups: Which waivers are due?

answers.answer: Retainage is a percentage (often 5 to 10) the customer holds back from every pay app until the job is closed out. Duracash holds it back on each pay app, shows it as a line, and tracks it as Held back, still owed until it's paid.
follow_ups: How do I get retainage released?
Which jobs are holding my retainage?

questions: How do I get retainage released?
How do I ask for retainage?
How do I get my retainage back?
How do I get retainage paid?
When do I get my retainage?
answers.answer: Retainage is paid at closeout. A job with retainage gets closeout paperwork: the items in the customer's Paperwork needed with each pay app that mention closeout, retainage or punch, or a closeout and punch list signoff if none do. Mark the job done, add those items (Open closeout paperwork), then tap Ask for retainage and confirm. Before the job is done you can ask for part of it on Money, Closeout (Part to ask for now). When the money arrives, tap Record retainage paid on the job.
follow_ups: Which jobs are holding my retainage?

answers.answer: Each customer has Days between follow-ups in Settings, Customer settings (7 if blank). Once that many days have passed since the pay app was sent (or since the last follow-up), Today shows a Follow up row and the job shows Send follow-up. Before then, Money, Unpaid shows the next follow-up date, and Follow up now on the job sends one early. Each follow-up is emailed to the customer's Email for pay apps and listed in the Outbox; from the third one it also copies Also email from the third follow-up.

questions: Where do I see unpaid pay apps?
answers.answer: Money, Unpaid lists every job with money owed: what is unpaid, days since it was sent, when it's due, when they said they'd pay, who to contact, and buttons to send a follow-up, email or call.
follow_ups: Who owes me money?

questions: Did the customer get my pay app?
Where do I see what I sent?
Who does the email come from?
answers.answer: Money, Outbox lists every email you approved and what happened to it: sent (with the time), failed (with the reason, such as an address the customer's mail server refused), or not sent. A failed or unsent email has a Send again button, and Today shows a Didn't go out row. Pay apps go out with the PDF and paperwork attached, from "your company via Duracash", and the customer's reply goes to whoever sent it. The demo account never sends real email.

No. Automated calls to customers need prior consent under federal law and are not planned before a lawyer reviews it. Money, Unpaid has a Call button that opens your phone, when the customer has a phone number.

questions: How do I import emails and texts?
How do I upload a document?
Can I bring in my paperwork?
How do I upload a file?
How do I upload a pdf or photo?
answers.answer:
Three ways:
- Drop files anywhere, or tap Take a photo or Add a file on a job (photos, PDFs, Word, Excel, CSV, saved emails). On a job page they go straight onto that job; elsewhere they wait in the Inbox.
- Paste an email, a text thread or your notes in the Inbox and tap Add to Inbox (or on a job, Add to job).
- Forward email and texts automatically once an owner connects an email service and a Twilio number (Inbox, Bring emails and texts in automatically).
The Inbox suggests the job from the job code, address, job name or sender; tap Add to (the job) to file it.
follow_ups: How do I import 30 days of notes?
How does it know which job?

questions: How do I import 30 days of notes?
answers.answer: Copy the notes, paste them in the Inbox with "Notes: one daily record per date" picked, and tap Add to Inbox. Start each day with a date (10/12, Oct 12, or 2026-10-12). Duracash splits them into one daily record per date and keeps the original date when you add them to a job.

questions: How does it know which job?
Why didn't it suggest a job?
answers.answer: It looks for the job code (like OAK), the job address, the job name, the customer's name, or an email from the customer's email for pay apps. If a few jobs fit, it lists them to pick from. Tip: put the job code in email subjects and texts. Tap Other job to change it before adding, and Undo under Recently added or dismissed takes an added item back off.

questions: How do I forward emails to Duracash?
answers.answer: Automatic email needs an email service that posts incoming mail to a web address (SendGrid, Mailgun or Postmark); automatic texts need a Twilio number. An owner opens Bring emails and texts in automatically in the Inbox for the private addresses to paste into those services. Until they're connected, save emails as .eml or paste them, and paste or screenshot texts.

questions: What file types can I upload?
answers.answer: PDF, JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, HEIC, Word (.doc, .docx), Excel (.xls, .xlsx), CSV, TXT and saved emails (.eml), up to 15 MB each. Drop the file on any page (on a job page it goes straight onto that job), or use choose files in the Inbox (Take a photo or Choose files on a phone). Web pages and SVG files are refused for safety.

questions: How do I log what happened today?
answers.answer: A daily record is a dated note of what happened on site: crew, work done, deliveries, problems. Go to Today, Daily record, pick the Job, type What happened today and tap Save to job record. Or paste many days at once in the Inbox as notes. They live on the job record and can be attached to a pay app's paperwork as backup.

Today, Calendar shows work complete, pay apps sent, follow-ups due, expected approvals, payments, waivers, finished jobs and pay app due dates. Pick a job in the Job filter to see only that job. Tap a day for its events. These are your billing dates, not legal deadlines.
follow_ups: Can I put this on Google Calendar?

questions: Can I put this on Google Calendar?
answers.answer: Yes. In Today, Calendar, open "Put these dates on your phone". On an iPhone or a Mac, tap Add to my phone's calendar. Or copy the private address, and in Google Calendar on a computer choose Other calendars, +, From URL. Outlook can subscribe to the same address. Calendar apps refresh it on their own schedule, often every few hours.

questions: When do I have to file a lien?
answers.answer: Not yet. Lien and notice deadlines depend on the state, your role and the project type, and a wrong date can cost lien rights, so Duracash won't calculate them until they're reviewed by a lawyer for a specific state. The calendar shows billing dates only.

questions: How do I export my data?
Can I get my data out?
answers.answer: An owner taps Export data in Settings, Company, under Your data, reset and delete. It downloads your company's jobs, customers, pay apps and records as one file. Photos and documents you uploaded are not in it, so keep your own copies of those.

An owner opens Settings, Company, Your data, reset and delete, and taps Reset data. Reset deletes every job, customer and record in your company; a snapshot is kept on the server first. To confirm, type the company name exactly and your password, then tap Reset everything. On the demo account, Reset the demo puts the sample data back.

On the sign-in screen, click Forgot your password? and enter your email: a reset link arrives that works once, for one hour, and signs you out everywhere else. Signed in, change it in Settings, My account. After 3 wrong passwords for one email, each new try has to wait a little longer, up to a minute. After 20 wrong passwords from one network, sign-in from that network pauses for 15 minutes. Passwords need at least 10 characters. If the server can't send email yet, the screen says so; ask the Duracash team.

Each company's data is kept separate; only your team's logins can open it, apart from the private links you share: the Calendar address and each customer's page. Owners decide who is on the team. Passwords are stored as one-way hashes; reset links work once and expire. Duracash is still early: keep your own copies of signed documents, and use Export data (Settings, Company) for a copy. Questions you ask here are saved so the team can add better answers.
This helper answers from a library of prepared answers and your own job data; it isn't an AI model. When AI features arrive, you'll approve everything they send.

Yes. On Money, Payments, open Import payments from QuickBooks (CSV), paste or choose a QuickBooks payments export (CSV or Excel) and tap Read payments: each payment is matched to its pay app where Duracash can tell (pick one from the Pick a pay app… list for the rest), and Record the ticked payments records the ones you tick. Or an owner taps Connect QuickBooks (when it is set up on the server): Then tap Read payments from QuickBooks, tick the ones to keep and tap Record the ticked payments. Duracash never changes your books. Each sent pay app also has Download for QuickBooks, a file QuickBooks imports as an invoice.
There are no direct connections to other software yet. Duracash sits beside the tools you use: export reports, photos or PDFs from them and drop the files into the Inbox.

The free trial is timed to the payment cycle: nothing to pay until the first pay app you send through Duracash is paid, or 90 days, whichever comes first (120 if a pay app is still unpaid on day 90). After the trial it is $299 a month, with no cut of what you collect. A company that bills homeowners in draws gets 45 days or the first paid draw. Today and Settings, Billing show where your trial stands. When billing is live, an owner taps Subscribe in Settings, Billing and pays by card through Stripe; if the Billing page says billing isn't live, there is nothing to pay.

questions: I need help from a human
answers.answer: Email the Duracash founders at the address under Contact at the end of the Privacy Policy (/privacy). Tell them what you clicked and what you expected; a screenshot helps. Questions you ask here are saved, so they also see what's missing.

questions: What does the Overview page show?
answers.answer: Today, Overview starts with Needs you: what to do next, most urgent first, each with its button. Below it are Done, not billed, Outstanding, Held back, still owed and Billed this month, how many jobs are active and how many can't be sent yet, then a table of jobs you can filter (Ready to send, Can't send yet, Unpaid, Waiver due, Completed this month). Hover a label and tap its (i) for what it means.

Each job has a short status, such as Needs paperwork, Blocked, Ready to send, Sent, Partly paid or Waiver due, and a line that names what's holding it up, for example "Conditional lien waiver is missing" or "Submitted, awaiting acknowledgment". It never just says pending. The Next column says what to do.
Settings, Activity log lists every action: what happened, when, who (the signed-in person) and what kind of action. Pick a job in the Job filter to see only that job.

questions: What are the little i icons?
answers.answer: Hover any label, column or tile: a small (i) appears next to it. Hover or tap the (i) to see what that field means. On a phone, each card has a "What do these mean?" list instead. Settings, Help has the full glossary.

questions: How do I finish a job?
How do I close a job?
Why can't I close this job?
answers.answer: An owner finishes a job. Finish job appears for an owner when the work is done and nothing is left: no open draft, no unsigned change order, nothing unbilled or unpaid, retainage paid and waivers sent. Until then the job page shows Before you can finish this job, one line per thing with a button for each. Tap Finish job and confirm: the job moves to Jobs, Job history and becomes read-only. An owner can tap Reopen job… there if a late payment comes in.

questions: How do I delete my account?
answers.answer: An owner can delete the company in Settings, Company, under Your data, reset and delete: type your password and the company name, then tap Delete everything. It removes every job, file, customer and record, and every user on the team, at once. Use Export data first if you want a copy. Server backups that already hold the data expire on their own (the newest 14 are kept by default).
follow_ups: How do I export my data?

questions: Do you back up my data?
What if the server loses my data?
answers.answer: Yes. The server makes a backup every 24 hours (and on start-up when the last one is older) and keeps the newest 14. Those copies sit on the server and guard against mistakes and bugs. When off-site backup is set up, each one is also encrypted and copied off the server. Keep your own copy with Export data too, and keep signed documents outside Duracash.
follow_ups: How do I export my data?

questions: Why do I need to confirm my email?
I didn't get the confirmation email
My emails say verify your email first
answers.answer: Duracash sends pay apps with replies coming back to the person who sent them, so it checks that the address is really yours first. Tap the link in the confirmation email (it works for 3 days). Didn't get it? Use Send the link again in Settings, My account, then check spam. Emails held while you were unconfirmed have Send again in the Outbox.

questions: Where are the terms of service?
What do you do with my data?
answers.answer: The Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy are linked at the bottom of the sign-in page (/terms and /privacy). In short: your data is yours, we use it only to run Duracash for you, we don't sell it or use it for advertising, the app loads no tracking scripts, and an owner can export or delete everything. Both pages say if they are still a draft awaiting a lawyer's review.
follow_ups: Is my data safe?
